1.question: Which genes are associated with Paget's disease of bone?
1.search_keyword: genes associated with Paget's disease of bone

final_answer.long_answer: Paget’s disease of bone has a clear genetic component. The vast majority of familial and many sporadic cases carry mutations in SQSTM1 (sequestosome-1/p62), which dysregulates NF-κB signalling in osteoclasts. Activating mutations in TNFRSF11A (RANK) lead to osteoclast hyperactivity and cause familial expansile osteolysis, an early-onset Paget-like disorder. Loss-of-function mutations in TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin, OPG) result in juvenile Paget’s disease by removing a key inhibitor of RANK-L signalling. Mutations in VCP (valosin-containing protein) produce inclusion-body myopathy with Paget’s and frontotemporal dementia, while rare variants in OPTN (optineurin) have also been linked to increased Paget’s risk. Together, these genes underscore the central role of RANK-NF-κB pathway regulation in the pathogenesis of Paget’s disease of bone.
